newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ruling party draws masses to final Mexico City rally.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party draws masses to final Mexico City rally.

text.p: Mexico's ruling party drew an estimated 75,000 people at the final campaign rally for its Mexico City mayoral candidate on Sunday, but not without resorting to traditional tactics to lure them.
Eight out of 10 people interviewed by Reuters at random at the rally for candidate Alfredo del Mazo, who trails about 20 points in the polls, said they had been obliged to attend.
"We didn't come of our own will. We plan to vote for a different party," said a young mother, who did not want to give her name.

Del Mazo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) faces competition for the city's top post for the first time in seven decades. Previously, Mexico City's mayor was hand-picked by Mexico's president.
Polls indicate the PRI faces not only defeat in the mayoral race on July 6, but also the loss of its majority in the lower house of Congress in the nation-wide vote.
But in Del Mazo's last public stand, the PRI resorted to traditional party politics to draw union members, labor leaders and street vendors in hoards to the nation's city center square.
To prove they attended, city workers picked up special tickets to hand over to their unions or street vendor organizations, which control key worker benefits and permits.

Despite his trailing in the polls, Del Mazo was adamant he would win the race and called on voters to remember that the PRI had forged modern Mexico. "Thanks to the PRI, Mexico has an important position in the world, stability and freedom," Del Mazo told the crowd.
Del Mazo painted the opposition as radical and politically inexperienced, specifically attacking Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, his rival from the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
"The opposition is not capable of ensuring your well-being. The reality is more complicated than they paint it, and the people of my city know it."

PRI militants said they would not stray from loyalties that has allowed the party to rule for 68 years. "I'm voting for the PRI. My family has always supported the PRI," laboratory worker Edilia Anorbe said.
But many workers at the rally said they were ready to break with tradition.
"I was at the PRD rally because I wanted to be," 33-year-old street vendor Alejandro Ruiz said. "Today I'm here because I have to be."
On Saturday, Cardenas drew about 100,000 supporters to the same square for his official campaign closing rally.
